official.deadline_note: The same 23 October 2026 14:00 CEST deadline applies to the application itself and to the reference letters; references will not be accepted after the deadline. The online application form has been available since late July 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027-28 academic year (fellowship starting 1 September 2027); application open from late July 2026 to 23 October 2026
official.status_note: The call for the 2027-28 academic year is open with an application deadline of 23 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST; the Centre offers up to 20 fellowships a year.
benefits: Basic grant of EUR 2,850 per month for a one-year residential fellowship at the Robert Schuman Centre, Villa Schifanoia

A household allowance of up to EUR 310 per month for fellows with a partner living with them in Florence, where the partner's income is below EUR 2,000 per month and the total does not exceed EUR 2,000 per month

A dependants allowance of EUR 210 per month for each dependent child living with the fellow in Florence (no allowance for children over 26, and a school or university certificate for those over 18 in full-time education)
EUR 650 for eligible research expenses, such as attendance at conferences

Reimbursement of the incoming trip to Florence and the outgoing trip at the end of the fellowship, up to a maximum of EUR 1,200 including both trips (first-class rail or economy air; taxi expenses are not reimbursed)
Reimbursement of visa costs (consular fees and travel to the nearest consulate) up to EUR 250 on supporting documents
Association with one of the Centre's projects or programmes, participation in its academic life and access to EUI postdoctoral programme activities
Fellowship grant reduced to a minimum of EUR 2,100 per month if the fellow receives other grants or salaries, which must be disclosed to the EUI
eligibility: Doctorate obtained more than five years prior to the start of the fellowship on 1 September; for 2027-28 the PhD should have been awarded before 1 September 2022
Open to post-docs, tenure-track academics and those wishing to spend their sabbatical at the Centre
Candidates of all nationalities are eligible
The research proposal must fit well with one of the Centre's main research themes, programmes and projects
Applicants whose doctorate was obtained less than five years ago are directed to the EUI Max Weber Programme instead
Fellows must live in the Florence area for the duration of the fellowship so that they can take an active part in the Centre's academic activities
requirements: Register the application early, inserting personal and referee details as soon as possible so referees can submit before the deadline
Submit the application by 23 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST
Provide the names of two academic referees and ensure at least two letters of reference are submitted online directly by the referees
Fellows must actively participate in the academic life of the Centre and contribute to the activities of the project or programme they are associated with
The research done during the fellowship should lead to a publication, as an EUI Working Paper, in a scientific journal or with a reputable academic publisher
documents: CV with a list of publications, in PDF
Letter of motivation (1-2 pages), in PDF
Two letters of reference submitted online by the referees (PDF, standard international fonts, no macros, special characters, password protection, electronic signatures or logos)
selection_criteria: Candidates are selected by the Academic Staff of the Robert Schuman Centre and their nomination needs to be approved by the Executive Committee of the EUI
Selection is based on the research proposal and the CV
The research proposal should fit well with one of the Centre's main research themes, programmes and projects
The decision is final and not subject to appeal, and no individual feedback is given on the research proposals of non-selected candidates; a reserve list may be drawn up
coverage: Basic grant of EUR 2,850 per month (minimum EUR 2,100 if other income is held)
Family allowances of up to EUR 310 per month for a partner and EUR 210 per month per dependent child
EUR 650 for eligible research expenses such as conference attendance
Reimbursement of incoming and outgoing travel up to EUR 1,200 and of visa costs up to EUR 250
application_method: Register the online application through the EUI OSIRIS portal (process JMF_APPLY), inserting personal and referee details early
Upload the CV with publication list, the letter of motivation, the research proposal and the passport copy
Contact the two nominated referees directly to confirm they received the automatic email request and will submit in time
Submit the application by 23 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST; reference letters may still arrive after submission but not after the deadline
official.application_route: Register early in the EUI OSIRIS online form, upload CV, motivation letter, research proposal and passport, nominate two referees, and submit before 23 October 2026 14:00 CEST.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to candidates of all nationalities; fellows must reside in the Florence area for the whole fellowship year
official.international_eligibility: Yes - all nationalities are eligible and the EUI assists non-EU fellows with visa and residence requirements
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The research proposal must fit one of the Robert Schuman Centre's main research themes, programmes or projects
official.research_requirement: A research proposal of 2-4 pages is a required document, and it must fit the Centre's research themes
official.duration: One year, 12 months from September to August; if a fellow arrives after the beginning of September or leaves before 20 July the grant is reduced or terminated, and no grant is paid for the month of August
official.description: The Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies at the European University Institute offers up to 20 one-year residential Jean Monnet Fellowships at Villa Schifanoia, Florence, to scholars more than five years past their doctorate who want to work within one of the Centre's research programmes.

not_confirmed: english_requirement - no English language requirement is published on the fellowship pages; references may be written in another language, though English guarantees the widest reading
tuition_coverage - no tuition element exists in the award, and none is published
verification.notes: Grant amount, family and dependants allowances, research expenses, travel and visa reimbursement, the absence of removal expenses, the insurance obligation, the deadline, the eligibility rule on the doctorate date, the required documents, the reference procedure, the Polish Jean Monnet Fellowship and the selection procedure were all read from the EUI's own Jean Monnet Fellowship pages (programme description, information for applicants, conditions of award, selection procedure).

applicant_utility.summary: The deadline is 23 October 2026 at 14:00 CEST and it applies to your referees as much as to you: reference letters submitted directly online by two academic referees are a hard requirement, and nothing is accepted late, so register your referee details weeks before you finish writing. Because the award is EUR 2,850 a month for twelve Florence months with no removal or installation allowance, you are moving a household on a fixed stipend and paying for your own medical insurance. Check the doctorate rule first: to apply for 2027-28 your PhD must have been awarded before 1 September 2022, and if you are inside that five-year window you belong in the Max Weber Programme instead.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Established researchers more than five years past the doctorate - tenure-track staff, postdocs on a second contract, or academics planning a sabbatical - whose project maps onto a Robert Schuman Centre programme.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify the doctorate date against the 1 September 2022 cut-off for the 2027-28 call
Register the application in OSIRIS as early as possible and nominate your two referees before polishing the proposal
Contact both referees personally to confirm they received the automatic request, since the EUI makes you responsible for chasing them
Pick a referee who is not a current full-time or part-time EUI professor, because such references are explicitly not accepted
Read the Robert Schuman Centre's research themes and name the programme or project your proposal feeds into
common_rejection_risks: Late or missing reference letters, which are not accepted after the deadline and cannot be replaced
A reference from a current EUI professor, which the EUI refuses to accept
A proposal that reads as generic rather than attached to one of the Centre's themes, programmes or projects
Being inside the five-year post-doctorate window, which routes you to the Max Weber Programme instead
Password-protected, macro-laden or non-standard-font PDFs, which the instructions specifically prohibit
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Removal and installation expenses have no provision at all; medical insurance must be either proven from your own scheme or bought through the EUI at your own expense; anything above EUR 1,200 of travel or EUR 250 of visa costs; and the grant is cut to a minimum of EUR 2,100 if you hold other income.
document_audit: The CV must include a list of publications, and the passport copy must be JPG rather than PDF
The motivation letter is capped at 1-2 pages and the research proposal at 2-4 pages, so resist appending a full paper
Reference letters must be plain PDFs with no electronic signatures or logos and no hard copies

Family allowances require documentary proof: a marriage certificate or proof of living together in Florence, birth certificates, and a school or university certificate for dependent children over 18 in full-time education
alerts: The grant is reduced if you arrive after the start of September or leave before 20 July, and no grant is paid for August, so a short-stay plan costs money
Fellows must live in the Florence area for the full year; this is a condition, not a suggestion
The decision is final with no appeal and no individual feedback, and a reserve list means an offer can arrive late if selected candidates decline
Polish candidates are automatically considered for the separate Polish Jean Monnet Fellowship awarded by the Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education
The EUI's AI-use guidance applies to the motivation letter and proposal: Generative AI must not autonomously write substantial parts, and any AI-generated content must be acknowledged
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in OSIRIS with referee details, upload the four documents, let the referees submit their letters online, then submit before 23 October 2026 14:00 CEST.
